title: I Let the Store Credit Policy Eat Their Own Coupon Book

parts.text: I scanned her expired coupon book and she demanded store credit anyway. I am twenty-four, cashier, holiday line, feet loud in my shoes. The book had a printed death date. My manager, Craig, had said honor smiles, not dates, except when he was mad. Today he was mad. The customer, Denise, had glitter on her sleeves from wrapping paper. The glitter kept landing on the scanner glass. Denise said, "You honored this last year" I said, "Last year it was alive" Craig hovered. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Craig is hovering, glitter is on the glass, and the coupon book's date is dead in print.

parts.text: I followed the date. Denise asked for Craig. Craig tried to override, then saw district in the line, a woman with a clipboard lanyard. He followed the date too. Denise left the glitter. I wiped the scanner with the blue cloth that always smells like alcohol and bananas somehow. Craig said I had made him look rigid. District said rigid is the policy he signed. I took my break in the break room with the buzzing light. I ate a granola bar that cracked too loud. The coupon book went in the reject drawer. I still find glitter in my pockets in January. District said, "What's the expiration" Craig said, "We're honoring dates today" A coworker hummed a carol off-key. It helped, against my will. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i.
